segmentation.text: walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
on the immediately adjacent highway to move around such an obstruction.
(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk
(b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic;
(c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;

elements.justification: As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: rel.occupies of a st.sidewalk while moving.
As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: a st.obstruction within the encounter reach (st.region_geometry) while on the sidewalk.
As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: a missing or impassable section is no object; nearest atoms with a gap.
'may proceed': the pedestrian is on the highway the sidewalk lies on (st.on_way) and off every sidewalk (rel.occupies).
As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: on the highway the sidewalk lies on, off every sidewalk, since leaving it at the obstruction.
'Such a pedestrian' refers back to the pedestrian of the admitted aggregate in that situation.

'walk ... as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk': the pedestrian's ground distance to the sidewalk it left (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'); st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, which s5 reads separately.

'a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; the pedestrian travels in it (rel.occupies).

'the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable': nearest atoms, a st.obstruction within the encounter reach of the pedestrian; an impassable area that is no object, and its lying between the lane and the sidewalk, have no atom: gap.

operationalizations.standard: as far to the side as possible
operationalizations.convention: Pedestrian detour width (HCM pedestrian space plus shy distance): the pedestrian's body stays within p.pedestrian_detour_offset of the sidewalk it left (st.region_geometry distance), one pedestrian width beside the sidewalk edge.

residues.why: A permission to travel against the direction of traffic; the duty to keep to the side near the sidewalk is the same whichever way the pedestrian walks.

applicability: As NRS_484B_297_6_o1: x is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian); for a sidewalk w (st.sidewalk) and a highway h (st.highway) with st.on_way w h, x occupies h and no sidewalk at this observation and has done so at every observation since an observation at which x occupied w, was moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution) and was within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of an obstruction (st.obstruction; st_region_geometry_distance). Exception (c): the duty does not apply where x occupies a st.bicycle_lane_or_path and an obstruction (st.obstruction) lies within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of x (nearest reading of 'the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable'; gap proposed).
obligation: x's ground distance to the sidewalk w it left (st_region_geometry_distance x w) is at most p.pedestrian_detour_offset.

narrowings.why: 'to move around such an obstruction' is read through leaving the sidewalk where the obstruction was encountered and staying off it since.
'as possible' is read as one fixed detour width beside the sidewalk; what is possible at the place (the obstruction's own extent into the highway) is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x leaves sidewalk w at a st.obstruction of kind barrier and walks on the roadway of h 4 m from w, outside any bicycle lane.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x leaves w at the barrier and walks 0.5 m from w until it returns to the sidewalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x walks on sidewalk w and never leaves it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.region_geometry is absent from the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x walks in a st.bicycle_lane_or_path 3 m from w while a st.obstruction lies within 1 m of x.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: carla_scene_graph acquisition standard: speed resolution of the recorded kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.obstruction_encounter_reach
param_proposals.convention: Encounter reach: the ground distance from a pedestrian's body to an obstruction within which the pedestrian has come up against it.
param_proposals.source: HCM pedestrian body ellipse and shy distance to fixed objects

param_proposals.name: p.pedestrian_detour_offset
param_proposals.convention: Pedestrian detour width: the largest distance from the sidewalk at which a pedestrian walking on the adjacent highway counts as keeping to the side nearest the sidewalk; one pedestrian design width plus shy distance.
param_proposals.source: HCM pedestrian space (body ellipse about 0.6 m by 0.5 m) plus shy distance

gaps.proposal: st.impassable_section | a stretch of a sidewalk, or of the ground between a sidewalk and the roadway, that a pedestrian cannot traverse because its surface is missing or blocked, carried as a region with a boundary and the way it lies on; decides where a pedestrian may leave the sidewalk and where it may travel | general
